title: Salade Niçoise
subtitle: Provençal salad with tuna, egg, and green beans
excerpt: The great composed salad of Nice: tuna, soft-boiled eggs, green beans, tomatoes, olives, anchovies, and a sharp vinaigrette, arranged separately rather than tossed. Bold and substantial.

recipe.sourceNotes: Salade niçoise takes its name from Nice on the French Riviera and has been documented since the late nineteenth century. The debate over what constitutes an authentic niçoise is one of the longest-running in French culinary culture. The Niçois themselves insist on raw vegetables (fresh tomatoes, young beans eaten raw, raw artichoke hearts) and tuna or anchovies preserved in oil, with absolutely no cooked vegetables and no potatoes. The version that spread globally through French restaurant culture in the twentieth century added cooked green beans and soft-boiled eggs and became the standard form. Many versions outside France also added cooked potatoes. The salad is always composed, never tossed: each component is arranged separately on the plate. A good niçoise vinaigrette is sharp, with more vinegar than a typical vinaigrette, to cut the richness of the tuna and eggs.

content.text: Soft-boil the eggs so the yolk is still slightly jammy in the centre: 7 minutes in boiling water, then immediately into iced water. The green beans should retain a slight crunch: blanch for 3 to 4 minutes in boiling salted water, then refresh in iced water. The salad is arranged on a large platter, with each component placed separately rather than mixed together. Dress lightly: each element should be moistened, not swimming.

items.preparation: 160 g tins in olive oil, drained

content.text: Whisk together the vinegar, mustard, salt, and pepper. Slowly whisk in the olive oil until emulsified. Make the dressing sharp and punchy.
Arrange the lettuce leaves on a large platter. Place the tomato wedges, green beans, and tuna in separate sections. Add the egg halves, olives, anchovies, and capers.
Drizzle the dressing over everything and serve immediately. Do not toss.
